reading.body:
Be My Eyes is a free accessibility service that pairs blind and low vision users with volunteers and companies over live video, and its AI product, Be My AI, describes images for those users.

The pattern here is a human network with an AI feature layered onto it, not an AI company that added a human fallback. The volunteer video service came first, and Be My AI extends the same task, describing what a camera sees, without a person on the other end. The stated audience is narrow and specific: blind and low vision users, with a minimum age of 17 attributed to the Perkins School for the Blind, and consumer terms applying.

For AI specifically, this is a case where the model runs on a phone camera and a network connection rather than in a data center the user ever thinks about. The compute is real but invisible, and the constraint the product faces is not power or buildings but accuracy on the user's behalf, since a wrong description of a scene is worse than no description. The data does not include usage numbers, model details, latency, or cost, so nothing here shows how much compute Be My AI consumes or where it runs.

What the data does not cover is equally important. It gives one product, one price point, one age limit, and one privacy note, all from the company's own materials. It says nothing about how the service is funded, how the AI is hosted, or how it performs, so it cannot support any claim about scale, growth, or infrastructure demand.

profile_text.body:
Be My Eyes describes itself as an accessibility technology company for blind and low vision people. According to its site, it connects blind or low vision users who want assistance with volunteers and companies across the world through live video and AI. The site also presents Be My AI, an image description tool, and shows an image credited as generated with Be My AI.

The company's product listing describes Be My AI as an AI image description tool for blind and low vision users. It is free to use under consumer terms, and users must be at least 17, a requirement tied to the Perkins School for the Blind. The site's own framing centers on pairing human volunteers with AI to deliver real-time assistance.

The available material does not include litigation, regulatory filings, or other third-party records for Be My Eyes.
